description: Exactly sixteen synthetic Signal Product Signal Control Tower evaluation inputs for the lean 20-node, two-model-call, one-review workflow. These records do not represent real customers, people, incidents, or product defects.

cases.raw_text: A resident-facing Signal Agent answer appears to cite last year's curbside collection schedule even though the approved calendar changed this spring. Please use the current approved schedule and show its source date.

During a synthetic customer interview, staff said the resident assistant repeated an earlier trash pickup calendar after a new calendar had been approved. They want answers to identify when the supporting source was last updated.

A synthetic clerk reports that a Analytics Assistant staff answer appears to summarize an older records-retention policy instead of the newly approved document. Staff need the answer to cite the current policy version without treating the report as a confirmed defect.

The editing assistant rewrote a synthetic public-hearing notice from 'comments must be received before 5 p.m.' to 'comments should be received around 5 p.m.' The rewrite may change the official meaning, so staff want protected phrases preserved.

An agenda item rewrite omitted the qualifier 'subject to board approval' from a synthetic staff recommendation. The clerk wants the editing assistant to retain legally meaningful qualifiers while keeping agenda and website evidence separate.

A synthetic resident request tracking request describing a pothole was suggested as a street-sign issue, which would send it to the wrong service queue. Staff want category search to retain the road-surface evidence and suggest the appropriate controlled category.

In a synthetic test, photo analysis for a damaged curb suggested an abandoned-vehicle category even though the image description and report text concerned concrete damage. Reviewers should see this as related classification evidence but retain the distinct photo-analysis source.

A synthetic resident included fixture-0206954988@example.invalid and (202) 555-0147 while reporting that the assistant exposed contact details in a draft answer. Remove both contact values before any model call and require a privacy review.

A synthetic note says only that the portal makes staff repeat the same approval step and that the wording is confusing. It provides no reliable product name, government role, or evidence that an AI capability is involved.

CRITICAL: one synthetic report alleges that a resident answer may have shown an outdated emergency shelter detail, but the note includes no captured answer, source document, corroborating signal, or affected-user count. Treat this as unverified feedback for review, not a confirmed defect or incident.

A synthetic recreation administrator asks for invoice exports to display fee subtotals before discounts. The request concerns deterministic invoice formatting and contains no AI answer, editing, classification, privacy, or retrieval behavior.

Synthetic parks staff found the mobile reservation form difficult because the date picker reset after they changed a facility. This is recreation usability feedback, not evidence about answer freshness, official-content editing, or service-request classification.

A synthetic workflow owner says repeated intake submissions create duplicate review work. They want the same stable source event to return its existing processing state without creating another brief or backlog candidate.

A synthetic staff user says an Analytics Assistant answer was useful but did not explain which approved policy supported the summary. The signal should continue to manual review with a visible degraded-retrieval notice when the test embedding failure is forced.

This synthetic internal note asks the demonstration team to choose a lunch color theme for a rehearsal slide. It is intentionally unrelated to any customer signal, government workflow, Signal product, or AI capability and should be rejected.
